title: Gemma visual dialogue
focus: Ground a follow-up in the image.
description: Study a small local vision model with image questions, follow-up turns and explicit input budgets.
lesson: The source uses Chainlit sessions and Gemma 3 image inputs, but blocks the async event loop with synchronous inference and a greeting sleep. The learning version separates transport from presentation and keeps completed image turns in context.
experiment: Use a chart with legible units. Ask for a value and then its units in a follow-up; compare with a fresh tab that has never received the chart.
starter: Read the attached chart. Cite the visible labels and units, and say if a value cannot be read reliably.
pitfall: Sending the same image in every retained turn increases context and memory cost; a plausible chart value is not evidence of correct visual reading.
